html:
Juan Manuel de Rosas was a rancher and general who ruled Buenos Aires Province, and in practice the Argentine Confederation, from 1829 to 1832 and from 1835 to 1852.

A rich cattle owner who commanded gaucho militias, he led the Federalists against the Unitarians of the cities, who wanted a central state. Given total power by the legislature, he ruled through a secret police, the Mazorca, which murdered opponents, and required everyone to wear the Federalist red. He fought off French and British blockades of the River Plate.

He was beaten at the Battle of Caseros in 1852 by the governor of Entre Ríos, Justo José de Urquiza, with Brazilian and Uruguayan help, and fled to England, where he died. His enemy Sarmiento wrote Facundo against him. He held Argentina together but delayed its constitution, written in 1853. His desert campaign of 1833 was a forerunner of the later Conquest of the Desert.
sum: Juan Manuel de Rosas was a rancher and general who ruled Buenos Aires Province, and in practice the Argentine Confederation, from 1829 to 1832 and from 1835 to 1852.
